reference: Metadata expectations use GNU Bash's documented type/help builtins and the published su usage/help contract. The util-linux su executable is not a safe or equivalent oracle for this builtin: its operations authenticate against host account services and change process identity, while bash-os su uses a kernel auth token. No operation parity is claimed.
coverage: Bash reports su as a registered builtin.
Bash help exposes the documented su invocation, password model, and kernel-token description.
Deferred operation coverage identifies parser, account-file, authentication, token, privilege-transition, child-execution, and terminal requirements for a disposable VM or injected mock.
exclusions: No su operation invocation is run. Authentication, token authorization, credential changes, target-shell execution, and PTY behavior require controlled private fixtures or a disposable VM.
No host account, password, shadow file, authorization device, or installed credential is accessed.
No GNU/util-linux su comparison is run because it would use host authentication and identity-changing behavior and does not implement the bash-os token contract.

cases.purpose: Verify that Bash resolves su as a builtin using the documented type -t metadata contract, without invoking su.

Check that the registered help text contains the declared invocation form and documented password and auth-token descriptions. The fixed marker is emitted only when all documented anchors are present.
cases.script:
PATH=
help su >help.txt
want_usage='su [--login|--no-login] [--keep-env] [-c CMD] [USER]'
usage=0
description=0
password=0
token=0
while IFS= read -r line; do
  case $line in
    *"$want_usage"*) usage=1 ;;
    *'Switch user with C-owned password verification.'*) description=1 ;;
    *'Argon2id PHC shadow format used by passwd.'*) password=1 ;;
    *'short-lived kernel auth token is minted and consumed internally'*) token=1 ;;
  esac
done <help.txt
[[ $usage == 1 && $description == 1 && $password == 1 && $token == 1 ]]
printf 'help contract anchors present\n'

cases.purpose: Exercise option parsing, default target selection, --, -c forms, extra arguments, invalid names, and exit/diagnostic behavior.
Check account lookup for present, absent, malformed, and unreadable synthetic passwd records, including target UID/GID/home/shell selection.
cases.reason: su reads PHCLIB_PASSWD/PHCLIB_SHADOW (su.c bsu_passwd_path/bsu_shadow_path) and BPW-style lock files under its lock dir, so account lookup, parsing and password verification run unprivileged on private files; the token mint (su.c bsu_kernel_proof) and credential drop happen only after verification. Absent/malformed/unreadable paths are implementable now; observing the selected UID/GID/home/shell needs the exec path, which needs guest /dev/bashos-auth v2 UAPI implementation (kernel module or a root-owned CUSE character-device mock implementing loadables/common/_bashos_auth_uapi.h: VERSION, PRIVCMD_AUTHZ, EXEC_VERIFY, EXEC_HANDOFF, token mint/consume, secret slots, policy info). The Debian guest kernel has no such device and the repository holds only the UAPI header, so open() fails with ENOENT and no unprivileged fixture can observe any ioctl behaviour (non-root) or guest case option to run a side as uid 0 inside a private mount namespace with fixture /etc/passwd and /etc/group bind-mounted (guest.py terminal.child_limits always drops to uid 2000; a drop to a second synthetic uid needs CAP_SETUID/CAP_SETGID, the legacy runner disables user namespaces, and an unprivileged user namespace maps only one uid) plus the device (root route also calls bsu_kernel_proof).

cases.purpose: Check correct and incorrect passwords, locked or malformed shadow entries, bounded password input, failure lockout, and success cleanup.
cases.reason: su reads PHCLIB_PASSWD/PHCLIB_SHADOW (su.c bsu_passwd_path/bsu_shadow_path) and BPW-style lock files under its lock dir, so account lookup, parsing and password verification run unprivileged on private files; the token mint (su.c bsu_kernel_proof) and credential drop happen only after verification. Verification and failure accounting are now observable via the PTY driver with OpenSSL-generated PHC vectors; only lock expiry timing and post-success cleanup are blocked.

cases.purpose: Check child exit and signal status propagation, fork/wait errors, parent-shell state preservation, and repeated invocation behavior.
cases.reason: Failure-status propagation, parent state preservation and repetition are observable now through the PTY verification-failure path; signal mapping and successful-child status need the device.

cases.purpose: Check tty password echo suppression and terminal restoration after success, read failure, and cancellation.
